title: Selective Delexicalization to Defend Structured-Output LLM APIs from Control-Plane Jailbreaks

contributions.purpose: Pinpoints where control-plane jailbreaks actually enter structured-output APIs so defenses can target the right component.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation analysis separating metadata removal from literal delexicalization in JSON schema sanitization.
contributions.evaluation: Ablation shows metadata removal alone provides no safety benefit while literal delexicalization achieves complete attack neutralization, identifying forced enum/const literals as the key attack vector.
contributions.source_quote: We identify forced enum/const literals as the key attack vector in control-plane jailbreaks, demonstrating through ablation that metadata removal alone provides no safety benefit while literal delexicalization achieves complete attack neutralization.

contributions.purpose: Defends structured-output APIs against control-plane jailbreaks without model retraining or inference overhead.
contributions.mechanism: Selective DeLex-JSON, a training-free schema sanitizer that flags suspicious forced literals via a conjunction-based heuristic (long values, whitespace, imperative verbs) and replaces them with opaque placeholders preserving schema structure.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 0% HarmBench attack success rate on both Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B (vs 22% ASR for EnumAttack without defense) with only 1.1% benign schema modification rate.
contributions.source_quote: We propose Selective DeLex-JSON, a training-free defense that achieves 0% HarmBench ASR on both Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B while incurring only 1.1% benign schema modification rate.

contributions.purpose: Shows the defense achieves safety at lower cost to benign usage than existing alternatives.
contributions.mechanism: Pareto comparison of DeLex-JSON against a Reject-Only baseline on safety and benign schema cost.
contributions.evaluation: DeLex-JSON Pareto-dominates existing defenses, reducing benign cost by 3.3 percentage points versus Reject-Only (1.1% modification vs 4.4% rejection rate) at identical safety guarantees.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that DeLex-JSON Pareto-dominates existing defenses, reducing benign cost by 3.3 percentage points compared to Reject-Only while maintaining identical safety guarantees.

contributions.purpose: Delimits the defense's coverage, showing where syntactic sanitization breaks down.
contributions.mechanism: Characterization of chunked-payload attacks that evade syntactic-level detection.
contributions.evaluation: Documents the limitation of syntactic-level defenses against chunked-payload attacks, motivating future semantic-level detection methods (no headline number reported on pages 1-2).
contributions.source_quote: We characterize the limitation of syntactic-level defenses against chunked-payload attacks, motivating future work on semantic-level detection methods.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Critically, existing work focuses on prompt-level attacks where adversarial content resides in the user input, whereas our work addresses a distinct attack surface in the schema specification.
